newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George sees A$140 mln in savings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George sees A$140 mln in savings.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said its A$2.65 billion friendly takeover of Advance Bank Ltd was driven by the need to lower costs and a review had found the merger could achieve a reduction of 15 percent in annual combined expenses or A$140 million before tax.
"Consequently, St George Bank anticipates that the transaction will increase its earnings per share before deducting goodwill amortisation," St George said in its merger announcement.
"The full merger cost savings are expected to be achieved within approximately 30 months," it said.

The combined bank, to be known as St George Bank, would have 7,913 employees and 607 branches upon completion of the merger in April next year, but St George chairman Frank Conroy there would be some staff redeployment and redundancies.
Conroy said the reduction in staff numbers would take place over several years, with staff to be retained on merit.

"Branch rationalisation will proceed only following a careful review of the suitability of St George Bank and Advance Bank branches in each area and the expected business activities of the merged bank," Conroy said.
"St George Bank expects to incur restructuring costs of A$50 million in the 12 months following closing of the merger," St George said in a statement.
"These costs will be accounted for as an adjustment to goodwill incurred in relation to the transaction and will not impact the underlying earnings of the Bank," it said.

St George Bank is due to release its 1995/96 (October/September) earnings in mid-November. It achieved first half net profit of A$74.52 million compared with A$66.90 million a year earlier. Operating profit rose to A$121.15 million from A$104.30 million. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
